questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** it depends on the boot. For the Blundstones he covers, he says not to treat pretreated styles out of the box, but to treat the distressed rustic ones. On frequency, he has no fixed schedule: he treats when the leather looks or feels dry.

**Out of the box**
- Reading Blundstone's FAQ, he says most Blundstones come pretreated, so the advice is not to treat them straight away [4].
- The exception is distressed leathers like Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black. They don't carry the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather [5].
- For his own rustic pair he recommends conditioning, and he doesn't recommend leaving them dry [6].
- He first assumed his distressed pair was already treated, then corrected himself after looking into it [5].
- He hasn't said whether this applies to boots from other brands.

**How often**
- His latest view (2022) is that he doesn't know the right interval and expects criticism whichever way he answers. He treats his boots when he feels they need it [1].
- He says to use your intuition. Treat when the leather looks dry, feels dry, or has stopped beading water [2].
- He also says to clean boots regularly, since dirt wears leather down faster [3].
- Back in 2019 he was more specific, saying you may have to wax them every month, maybe every week if you're really hard on them [7].
- That same year he said any leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should be conditioned [8].

**Tip:** when you do treat them, he says to clean first, then condition, then wax [9]. He also says to start with little coats instead of oversaturating [10].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, but mostly the first time they get wet. He treats the first hot soak as the shrinking step, and the waist is where you feel it. After that they loosen with wear. He hasn't said anything about them keeping on shrinking with later washes.

**Newest take (2023):** His shrunk 501 STFs ended up smaller than regular rinsed 501s. He says the difference is small if you wash them similarly, and he bets frequent wear would stretch them out to about the same size. He also says to avoid very hot water and the dryer, because that is how you get a really nice fit. [1][2]

**Sizing to allow for it:** In 2025 he still says you should usually go two sizes up. [3] In 2021 he said Levi's advice is correct: size up two in the waist and two inches in length, and then the pants fit regularly after you get them wet. [4][5]

**Where it shrinks:** In his 2019 soak, the jeans slimmed up mainly around the waist, and the length barely changed. [6][7]

**After wearing them:** In 2020, after a year, he said his pair was a really good fit. He had bought a 29 waist and could barely pull them on at first. [8] He also said he would have gotten a longer length, a 32. [8]

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** applying his rule to your 33x30, he'd have you buy about a **35 waist x 32 length** in the 501 STF. He hasn't covered the 502 or how it compares to the 501, so that's his 501 rule applied to your numbers, not a 502-to-501 conversion.

**His rule (most recent first):**
- In his 2025 value ranking he says of the 501 STF that you should usually go two sizes up. [1]
- In his 2021 LVC video he says Levi's advice is correct: size up two in the waist and two inches in length. His example is that a 34 wearer should get a 36, though he adds he doesn't think a 36 exists. [2] So a 35 may not be offered in your size. He doesn't say what to do then.
- In his 2023 Wrangler comparison he followed this himself, going from a 30 to a 32 in the shrink-to-fit pair. [3]

**He changed his mind on this.** In 2019 he ignored Levi's advice and bought a 29x30. [4] By 2021 he said it took him several pairs to realise Levi's was right. [2] In 2020 he said that pair was nearly impossible to pull on at first, though it fit well after a year of wear. He also said he'd have gotten a 32 length, and he cuffed them anyway. [5]

**Why size up:** the jeans shrink when soaked, so he says they fit normally once wet. [2]

**With boots (late 2019):** He says he always used to cuff his jeans but now likes them down over his boots more [3].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly yes, but he's since hedged.** In late 2022 he said the 3335s beat the 1907s. By September 2023 he said they "still might be" his favorite Red Wings, though he also said the 1907s have qualities he really likes, and he was selling the 3335s.

**Most recent (Sept 2023):**
- He says he's on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time, and that they "still might be" [1].
- He adds that the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [1].
- He likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight, and nimbleness [2]. He finds them easier for walking or a light hike [2].
- Even so, they were on his sell list [3].

**Oct 2022:**
- He called the 3335s his favorite boots he's ever had and said they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [4].
- He explained that he's not doing heritage work, just hiking and walking in the woods, so he finds them a dramatically better all-around boot [5].
- He added that the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so anyone who needs a tough boot should probably look elsewhere [5].

**Earlier (Sept 2021):** Before he had the 3335s, he called the 1907s Red Wing's best heritage boots by far and told viewers to get them if they were looking at a moc toe Red Wing [6].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, he's still a big Blundstone fan, even though he's retiring his own 585s. The retirement is part of a big cull of his boot collection, not a sign he's gone off the boots.

**Late 2023 (Sept):** He calls Blundstones "just incredible" and says he's "a big fan" who has "always loved them." He notes some people really don't like them [1]. He still says it's time to retire them [1]. The video is about cutting down his collection, in his words "destroying it for the greater good (donating, selling, etc.)" [3].

**Earlier (June 2022):** His view was the same. He asked whether Blundstones are worth the hype and answered "I think so!" He said he loves them and that they're still some of his favorites, though they're not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [4].

So his opinion hasn't really changed. He still rates them highly, and the 585s are being retired after heavy wear.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He leans toward Solovair over the Made in England Dr. Martens, and he still liked his Solovairs in 2023 despite some problems. His case is mostly about value. He thinks Made in England Docs are really for big Dr. Martens fans.

**Latest view (2023)**
- In his 2023 England vs. Thailand video, he says the Made in England 1460 isn't objectively worth the extra $90: "i'd say probably not" [1]. He says that right now "you have to be a mega fan to get them" [2].
- In his boot-collection cull later that year, he says of his Solovair monkey boots that "through all of that I really like these boots" [3]. He says they feel too roomy, which he thinks probably means he sized wrong, and he would sell them "only to get another pair of monkey boots" [3].

**His original comparison (2022)**
- **Price:** Solovairs are cheaper than Made in England Docs [4]. He says much of the extra cost of the England versions is paying for the "made in england part" [5].
- **Leather and midsoles:** He says the Made in England Docs' better leather "will age fine" and is probably on par with Solovair. He says the same of the better midsoles [6].
- **Comfort:** Solovairs have a shank, which makes them "a bit more comfortable over long periods of time" [7]. He says Docs are easier to break in, while Solovairs are tougher at first but more comfortable down the line [8].
- **Repair:** He says Solovairs are Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they are easier to resole [9].
- **Maker:** He notes Solovair is a much smaller company and one of the original makers of the Doc Martens boot. He says the eight-eye Derby is essentially the same boot [6].
- **Where Docs win:** Solovair doesn't do the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Docs [10].

**Caveat: quality control**
He had a Solovair defect: after eight wears a back tab ripped off and a lace snapped. He assumed it was a manufacturing defect [11]. In 2023 he mentions the quality-control problem again and says Solovair sent the wrong parts and told him to repair it himself [3]. He still came out liking the boots.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't said anything about multi-day hikes, so there's no direct verdict on a 4-day trip. His closest advice suggests Blundstones are fine for day hikes and casual use but not ideal for serious hiking.

**Ankle support:** In his one-year review (2020) he said the boots "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. He still took them up and down a few mountains in Maine, where they got scuffed but "held up well" [1]. He also says they are decent for work but not anything incredible [2]. If your hike is rough or mountainous, that points against them.

**Blisters:** His new pair gave him no blisters on a first walk through the city and woods [3]. Later, when he started running and walking track in them, he got "big fat gross blisters" that stopped after two to three weeks of use [4]. Over four days, a pair that isn't fully broken in could be a risk.

**Water:** He describes them as water resistant, not waterproof. You can get them wet, "but don't go swimming in them because water's gonna come in" [5]. They need regular treatment to stay that way [6]. In his 2023 video he calls his heavily worn pair "probably my most water resistant boots" [7].

**What he reaches for:** He keeps lace-up hiking boots such as the Keens for hiking [8]. He describes Blundstones as shoes he can "just kind of flop on really quick" for errands or rain [9].

**Bottom line:** Going by his comments, he'd see Blundstones as fine for easy walks and short hikes, but would doubt them for four days, mainly because of the lack of ankle support and the risk of blisters. That is my reading of his rules, not something he said about multi-day trips.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Based on his newest t-shirt roundup (2025), the Uniqlo tee at about $20 is his best value, but for someone taller or wider he steers you to Muji. He hasn't given a size recommendation for a 5'11", 225 lb build, so I can't name a size for you.

**Best value for a bigger guy: Muji**
- He calls the Uniqlo shirt, at about $20, probably the best t-shirt you can get "bar none for the price" [1].
- He adds that if you're taller or wider, you'd want Muji instead. It costs about $4 or $5 more but is significantly longer and a good deal wider, and he says you'd probably like it if you're a little bigger [2].
- Earlier in 2025 he said Muji's extra ~$10 over Uniqlo feels justified, with a thicker, tighter collar and a nicer feel [3].

**If you'll spend a bit more**
- House of Blanks, about $35, is a combed ringspun tee cut and sewn in Canada with zero torquing. He calls it an outstanding value [4].
- The 3Sixteen two-pack, about $49, he calls probably the best deal in the mid-range [5].

**Sizing**
- He doesn't tie any shirt to a size for your build.
- He says he personally likes a lot of space across the shoulders in a tee [6].
- On the Los Angeles Apparel tee, he said sizing down one might make it a winner [7]. That is advice about that brand's fit, not about your size.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
He won't name one best t-shirt, but he does pick a favorite in each category, so you can use those. His newest video says the best shirt "just has to line up with your preferences" [1], and he says all the shirts in it are winners [2]. Here is the pick-this-one version of his advice.

**If you want just one: J. Press x American Trench.** It sits in his "I would recommend this t-shirt to absolutely anybody" category [3]. When he had to choose in that category, he went with it for the rougher hand feel and more structure [4].

**If you want three, add a value pick and a nicer pick:**
- **Front General Store (about $40, made in Japan).** In his best-value category he says "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [5]. If you prefer a perfectly smooth shirt with no twisting, he'd say House of Blanks instead [5].
- **Merz b. Schwanen (MSB).** In his "Supremes" category he gives the edge to MSB "today", with Lady White close behind [6]. He likes its smoother yarn and its distinctive fit across the neck and chest [6].

**Other options he named:**
- **Cheapest:** The $20 Uniqlo is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [7]. It is open-ended and a bit rough. If you're taller or wider, he says to get Muji instead, which is longer and wider [8].
- **Japanese shirt:** Wonder Looper is his favorite in the Japanese category because it has a more universal fit than the cropped, wide Samurai [9].
- **Heavyweight:** American Giant is his pick, because it's a little lighter and fits more universally [9].

His earlier videos named single winners. In 2024 he gave Asket the overall prize [10].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** the 1907 is a storm-welted boot and the 875 is Goodyear welted. He says that if you're buying a Red Wing moc toe, get the 1907. His own all-time favorite Red Wing is a different boot, the 3335.

**Welt construction**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts durable and "pretty water resistant", and says the welt leaves room for a cork footbed that molds to your foot [1].
- The 1907 has a storm welt, which Red Wing sometimes calls "Norwegian like" [2]. He says the popular view he's seen on Reddit is that Red Wing's version just stitches an extra strip of leather onto the welt. He isn't quite sure about that [3].

**Price and value**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875. He argues that's effectively no extra cost, because the 1907 includes Red Wing's removable leather footbed (typically about $40 on its own), the storm welt, and a pair of leather laces (typically about $15) [4].
- The removable footbed also lets you pull it out to help the boots dry [4].

**What they share**
- Both come with crepe soles, which he doesn't really like [2]. In 2022 he said the crepe on the 875 and 1907 will break down faster than the dense Vibram sole on the 3335 [5].
- He also calls both of them more beefily constructed than the 3335, so they're the better pick if you need a tough boot [6].

**His verdict**
In the 2021 video he calls the 1907 Red Wing's best heritage boot "by far" and says to get it if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing [2]. By 2022 his favorite boots were the 3335s, which he said beat both the 1907s and the 875s for his hiking and woods-walking [6].

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his newest ranking (Sept 2025), Uniqlo's $20 tee is the best budget t-shirt you can get for the price. Front General Store costs more but is the one he says he'd personally pick for character. He covered Pro Club and Hanes only in 2024, and he rates them below both.

**Uniqlo (his value pick)**
- In 2025 he says its $20 tee is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price." [1]
- He calls it open-ended, a bit rough, and "your starter t-shirt." If you're taller or wider, he points to Muji instead. [2]
- In June 2025 he praised the $15 version, noting the bound neck collar so it doesn't wiggle. [3]
- In 2024 he said the Uniqlo heavyweight crew "may be" the best bargain tee. [4]

**The Front General Store (the step up)**
- It's his personal pick in the budget category. He's 'feeling' it that day and says he might choose House of Blanks another day. [5]
- He describes the $40 shirt as 100% made in Japan, with great proportions and feel. [6]
- In 2024 he called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get," with a 6/10 softness score. [7]
- It costs about twice as much as Uniqlo. That's why Uniqlo stays his value pick.

**Pro Club**
- He covered it only in 2024. He liked everything about it, but it was the roughest shirt on that list. [8]
- He gave it 4/10 for softness. [8]

**Hanes**
- Also from 2024: he calls it a classic $10 shirt, scoring 7/10 for softness. [9]
- He found it much softer than Pro Club and lighter in weight. [10]
- In 2025 he lumps Hanes-type mass-market brands with Gildan. Their very low prices come with defects: all five shirts he had from these brands had one. [11][12]

**Bottom line**
- Cheapest good option: Uniqlo.
- If you want more character and a Japan-made shirt for around $40: Front General Store.
- He hasn't said anything newer on Pro Club.

questions.question: Would you recommend this [Barbour Bedale] or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
**He'd lean Barbour for this mix of rain, wind and light spring wear, but he hasn't compared the two directly.** The Flint and Tinder is a strong alternative if you want a lined jacket for less money.

**Barbour**
- In his 2025 ranking he calls its 6 oz Sylkoil "the lightest weight fabric" of the jackets he covered. [1] He says that flexibility means "you could toss on your Barber and be super comfortable" in any season. [2]
- It has a throat latch, hood snaps and storm cuffs, which he calls helpful in bad weather. [3] In his first Bedale review he also liked the storm flap that stops water running through the zipper. [4] He strongly suggests buying the hood. [5]
- On rain, he says it's "not a designated rain jacket". [6] A freshly waxed one didn't leak in his shower test, but he says how water resistant it is "depends on what stage your jacket is in with the wax". [7] As the patina builds and wax wears off, it loses some water resistance. [8] In 2021 he compared it with the Taylor Stitch Winslow parka and said the Barbour suits "a brisk walk to your car" more than long stretches in the rain. [9]
- He says thornproof finishes add wind resistance. [10] He hasn't said how the Sylkoil version handles wind, or whether the Bedale is one or the other.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker**
- He says it's built for everyone and "not crazy lightweight, but it is a lighter weight, so it's comfortable". [11] He also notes that it's lined. [12]
- At $300, US-made, with Martexin fabric, he says it's hard not to recommend. [13]
- That section of the video was sponsored by Huckberry, so treat the praise accordingly. He says he'd talked about the jacket many times before the sponsorship. [14]
- He doesn't say how it performs as a rain jacket or windbreaker.

**Bottom line:** For a light spring jacket that also copes with showers and wind, his comments favor the Barbour. It's the lighter jacket, and it has the storm-weather details. Keep it freshly waxed if rain matters to you. If you'd prefer a lined jacket at a lower price, the Flint and Tinder is one he recommends widely.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
His con is a personal preference, not a claim that Huckberry only makes unlined jackets. By 2025 he was praising the lined Flint and Tinder trucker and had softened on unlined jackets in general. He hasn't said anything about a flannel-lined version in the videos available here.

**The 2025 view (newest)**
- He describes the Huckberry Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker as lined, "so that way it's comfortable. You don't get wax on your skin." [1] He also mentions a wool-lined version he hasn't tried yet, which he says is heavier all around. [1]

- He has also softened on unlined jackets. He says he usually wants a liner on a wax jacket because the wax gets on your skin, but "in my old age" he "kind of see[s] why you wouldn't line something." [3][4]

**The 2023 con**
- In the waxed jacket comparison, he called the Huckberry trucker the cheapest, simplest unlined jacket in the group. [5] The con he stated was that Huckberry and Rogue Territory jackets "are not lined." [6]
- His reason was personal: he always likes a lining on wax jackets so the wax isn't touching your clothes or your arms. [6]

**What he hasn't covered**
He doesn't mention a flannel-lined Huckberry trucker. He also doesn't say whether the 2023 unlined jacket and the lined 2025 jacket are the same line.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s and the 875s, but he does give sizing advice for the 3335s and some related comments on Red Wing moc toes.

**3335s:** He went true to size and they fit fine [1]. But they have a slim profile with a thin outsole, and they taper down [2]. With thin cotton socks he had no tightness. With wool socks his toes felt squished and he couldn't wiggle them much [3].

**Red Wings in general (not 875-specific):** In his 1907 video he says he usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and they fit perfect [4]. His rule is to buy leather boots snug, not squished [5].

**Moc toes like the 875:** He calls the Red Wing moc toe's toe box a little large [6]. In another video he describes a very blocky, high toe wall [7]. That contrasts with the slim, tapered 3335, but he doesn't say it as a fit comparison, so treat it as a rough inference.

He hasn't covered the 875's sizing or fit directly in the videos available here.
